**1 — Scene:** A small pile of what appears to be battered or egg-coated, skin-on fried fish, with leafy greens, pine nuts and a little red pepper. Identification is somewhat uncertain.

**2 — Vessel:** Large, rounded-square dinner plate, partly cropped. Using an equivalent circular diameter of **28 cm**, its estimated area is **3.14 × 14² = 615 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Fried coated fish pieces; spinach-like leaves; scattered pine nuts; red pepper garnish. Cooking oil appears incorporated into the fish coating, so it is included in that item’s energy estimate.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = gross volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Coated fried fish | 22% | 135 cm² × 1.6 cm = 216 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 205 g | 250 | 513 kcal |
| Leafy greens | 4% | 25 cm² × 1.5 cm = 37 ml | 0.15 g/ml | 6 g | 23 | 1 kcal |
| Pine nuts | 1% | 6 cm² × 0.7 cm = 4.3 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 3 g | 675 | 20 kcal |
| Red pepper | 0.5% | 3 cm² × 0.5 cm = 1.5 ml | 0.6 g/ml | 1 g | 31 | <1 kcal |

The allocated areas total **27.5% of the plate**, consistent with the substantial empty space.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **215 g and 535 kcal** is plausible for several coated fish pieces with only a few leaves and scattered nuts. The fish identification and amount of absorbed oil are the main uncertainties.
